note: Curated tours of the history map. Each is a URL (/history/?chapter=<id>). The blurbs say what the period is, in one sentence, and make no claim the movements do not carry.

chapters.title: The first Islamic conquests
chapters.blurb: From Muhammad's death in 632 the Rashidun and Umayyad armies take Syria, Egypt, Persia and North Africa, and Arab settlers follow into the garrison cities.

chapters.title: The Viking age
chapters.blurb: Norse raiders, traders and settlers reach Britain, Ireland, the Rus lands and Iceland, and one voyage reaches North America around 1000.

chapters.title: Crusaders and the Levant
chapters.blurb: The First Crusade of 1099 founds the crusader states on the Levantine coast; the Ayyubids and Mamluks win them back by 1291.

chapters.title: The Mongol conquests
chapters.blurb: From the 1206 gathering of the Mongols the armies cross Asia and reach Hungary, Persia, Russia and China.

chapters.title: The rise of the Ottomans
chapters.blurb: From a small frontier state to an empire holding the Balkans, the Levant, Egypt and North Africa.

chapters.title: The age of discovery and conquest
chapters.blurb: Portuguese and Spanish ships open the Atlantic and the Indian Ocean, and conquest and settlement follow in the Americas, Africa and Asia.

chapters.title: The Atlantic slave trade
chapters.blurb: Millions of enslaved Africans are carried across the Atlantic; the atlas records where they were taken from and where they were sent.

chapters.title: Napoleon and the reshaping of Europe
chapters.blurb: French armies redraw the map from Spain to Russia, and the Congress of Vienna draws it back.

chapters.title: The great emigrations
chapters.blurb: Famine, persecution and opportunity send tens of millions across oceans, and indentured labourers across the Indian Ocean and Pacific.

chapters.title: The partition of Africa
chapters.blurb: European powers divide almost the whole continent in a generation.

chapters.title: The world wars
chapters.blurb: Invasions, occupations, deportations and flight across Europe and Asia.

chapters.title: Partition and decolonisation
chapters.blurb: Borders redrawn, populations exchanged and expelled, empires ended.

chapters.title: Refugees since 1990
chapters.blurb: Wars in the Balkans, the Middle East, Africa and Ukraine send millions across borders.

chapters.title: Mass mortality
chapters.blurb: Epidemics, famines, genocides and massacres: black outlines on the years and places where deaths were hardest to record.
